scheme_name: Sharodotsav Pandit Nandan Mehta: Plan for Conducting Classical Music Competition and Ceremony
description:
The Sharodotsav Pandit Nandan Mehta scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to promote classical music and cultural heritage. 

This scheme was officially launched on October 2, 2021. 

It is named after the renowned classical musician Pandit Nandan Mehta, who made significant contributions to Indian classical music. 

The primary objective of the Sharodotsav scheme is to foster the appreciation and practice of classical music among the youth. 

The scheme aims to conduct an annual classical music competition that showcases the talents of young musicians across the country. 

The competition is designed to identify and promote emerging artists in the field of classical music. 

The scheme also seeks to create a platform for these artists to perform and gain recognition. 

The government has set a target of engaging at least 10,000 participants in the first year of the competition. 

The competition is expected to be held in various phases, culminating in a grand finale event. 

The grand finale is scheduled to take place in the month of December each year. 

Participants will be judged based on their performance quality, technical skill, and creativity. 

Winners of the competition will receive cash prizes and certificates of recognition. 

The first prize is set at INR 1,00,000. 

The second prize will be INR 50,000. 

The third prize will be INR 25,000. 

In addition to the cash prizes, winners will also receive opportunities for mentorship from established musicians. 

The scheme aims to provide a total budget of INR 5 crore for the first year of implementation. 

This budget will cover the costs of organizing the competition, including venue rentals, marketing, and prize distribution. 

Eligibility for participation in the Sharodotsav competition is open to individuals aged between 15 and 30 years. 

Participants must demonstrate proficiency in one or more forms of classical music, including Hindustani or Carnatic styles. 

There are no specific educational qualifications required to participate in the competition. 

However, participants must submit a video audition as part of the application process. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, interested candidates must visit the official website dedicated to the Sharodotsav scheme. 

They will need to fill out an online application form with personal details and contact information. 

Candidates must upload their video audition, which should not exceed five minutes in length. 

The deadline for submitting applications is typically set for November 15 each year. 

After the application deadline, a panel of judges will review the submissions. 

Shortlisted candidates will be notified by November 30. 

These candidates will then be invited to participate in regional rounds of the competition. 

The regional rounds will take place in various cities across India during the month of December. 

The grand finale will feature the top performers from these regional rounds. 

The final event will be held in a prominent venue, which will be announced in advance. 

The event will also include performances by established classical musicians as part of the ceremony. 

The implementing authority for the Sharodotsav scheme is the Ministry of Culture, Government of India. 

The ministry is responsible for overseeing the organization and execution of the competition. 

Contact details for the Ministry of Culture can be found on their official website. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote Indian classical arts and culture. 

It aligns with the government's vision of preserving and promoting India's rich cultural heritage. 

The government aims to increase public engagement with classical music through this initiative. 

Statistics indicate that participation in cultural events has been on the rise in recent years. 

The Sharodotsav scheme is expected to further enhance this trend. 

In addition to the competition, there will be workshops and seminars conducted for participants. 

These sessions will focus on various aspects of classical music, including performance techniques and music theory. 

The scheme also aims to collaborate with music institutions and universities across India. 

This collaboration will help in reaching a wider audience and encouraging more participants. 

The government plans to document the performances and create an archive of the event. 

This archive will serve as a resource for future generations interested in classical music. 

The Sharodotsav scheme is expected to have a positive impact on the music community. 

It will provide a platform for young musicians to showcase their talent. 

The initiative will also contribute to the cultural vibrancy of the nation. 

The government encourages local communities to support the competition by attending events. 

This support will help in creating a culture of appreciation for classical music. 

The scheme is expected to receive media coverage to promote awareness and participation. 

Social media campaigns will also be launched to engage with a younger audience. 

The overall goal of the Sharodotsav Pandit Nandan Mehta scheme is to ensure that classical music continues to thrive in India. 

By providing opportunities for young artists, the government aims to keep the tradition alive. 

The scheme represents a significant investment in the cultural future of the country. 

It is a step towards recognizing the importance of arts in national identity. 

The first edition of the competition is anticipated to set a precedent for future events. 

The government hopes to expand the scope of the competition in subsequent years. 

This expansion may include additional categories or forms of music. 

The Sharodotsav scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to cultural preservation. 

It reflects the belief that music is a vital part of Indian heritage. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to inspire a new generation of classical musicians. 

The scheme is poised to become a landmark event in the Indian cultural calendar. 

In conclusion, the Sharodotsav Pandit Nandan Mehta scheme is a comprehensive initiative aimed at promoting classical music in India. 

With specific objectives, benefits, and a structured application process, it is designed to engage young musicians and foster their talents. 

The scheme not only honors the legacy of Pandit Nandan Mehta but also contributes to the ongoing celebration of Indian classical music.
